sources.summary: Court record (High Court of South Africa, Gauteng Local Division sitting as an Equality Court, case 2024/070075, judgment 10 November 2025) in Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre (Medium B): the landmark ruling for a trans inmate against the Department of Correctional Services - refusal of gender expression (feminine attire, she/her pronouns), inadequate accommodation and denial of state-funded gender-affirming hormone therapy held to be unfair discrimination; hormone therapy recognised as part of the constitutional right to adequate medical treatment under section 35(2)(e).

Legal Resources Centre case page (14 November 2025): summary of the High Court ruling for a transgender inmate against the Department of Correctional Services - unfair discrimination and harassment by refusing feminine clothing and correct pronouns and appropriate accommodation; the court held gender-affirming hormonal therapy must be provided at state expense and ordered the department to implement its own SOPs for transgender inmates immediately.

Human-rights commission / National Preventive Mechanism media statement (14 November 2025): welcomes the 10 November 2025 High Court ruling in Mokoena v Head of Johannesburg Correctional Centre (case 2024/070075); describes the OPCAT monitoring mandate over places of deprivation of liberty, the inmate's account (initially allowed to express her gender, later restricted from feminine clothing and make-up, misgendered, denied prescribed hormone therapy, DCS arguing it was cosmetic), and the court's finding that gender-affirming healthcare forms part of adequate medical treatment under section 35(2)(e) of the Constitution.
